filings.business_description: Cal-Maine sells shell eggs across conventional and specialty categories, including cage-free, organic, and free-range eggs, to retail and foodservice customers nationwide. It also sells prepared foods such as egg patties, omelets, pancakes, waffles, and specialty wraps. The filing identifies three reportable product segments: Conventional Shell Eggs, Specialty Shell Eggs, and Prepared Foods; it also describes other operations, including co-pack shell eggs and egg products, that are not reportable segments. It sells through grocery and club stores, other supermarket-serving companies, and foodservice distributors, and prices shell eggs using market-based, cost-based, or hybrid arrangements.
filings.risk_factors_summary: Wholesale shell egg prices are volatile and outside the company’s control, exposing revenue and profits to supply, demand, and seasonal changes. Feed is the largest element of shell egg production cost, and feed prices are affected by factors including weather, supply and demand, trade policies, and geopolitical instability. HPAI outbreaks can require depopulation and disrupt production; the filing reports a March 2026 outbreak at the company’s Maryland pullet facility. Customer concentration is significant: the top three customers represented 43.1% of fiscal 2026 net sales, and Walmart accounted for 30.0%. The filing also identifies prepared-food acquisition integration and changing consumer preferences as risks; technology-specific risks are not available in provided sources.
filings.mda_highlights: Fiscal 2026 net sales were $2.9 billion and net income was $316.7 million. Net sales decreased 31.7% from fiscal 2025, primarily as conventional shell egg prices fell while the layer population recovered from HPAI-related disruption. Average conventional shell egg price per dozen declined 50.9%; prepared foods contributed $244.8 million, or 8.4%, of fiscal 2026 net sales, primarily following the Echo Lake Foods acquisition. Management attributed the recent decline in wholesale egg prices primarily to improved supply and reduced panic-driven purchasing and retailer and foodservice inventory builds. Item 7 describes a change to three reportable operating segments effective in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026; further information about accounting-policy changes, going-concern language, or capital raises is not available in provided sources.

citations.claim: 10-K Item 1: The company sells shell eggs in conventional and specialty categories to retail and foodservice customers.
citations.excerpt: The Company’s shell egg portfolio spans the full egg value ladder—from conventional to specialty, including cage-free, nutritionally enhanced, organic, brown, pasture-raised, and free-range eggs—serving both retail and foodservice customers nationwide.

citations.claim: 10-K Item 1: Prepared Foods includes the production and sale of prepared egg and other food offerings.
citations.excerpt: The Prepared Foods segment consists primarily of the production, packaging, marketing and distribution of prepared foods product offerings such as pre-cooked egg patties, omelets, folded and scrambled egg formats, pancakes, waffles and specialty wraps.

citations.claim: 10-K Item 1: The company has three reportable product segments and other nonreportable operations.
citations.excerpt: As a result, we identified three reportable segments: Conventional Shell Eggs, Specialty Shell Eggs, and Prepared Foods.

citations.claim: 10-K Item 7: The company sells to retail and foodservice-related customers.
citations.excerpt: We sell our products to a diverse group of customers, including national and regional grocery store chains, club stores, companies servicing independent supermarkets in the U.S., and foodservice distributors serving restaurants, convenience stores, healthcare and education facilities, and hotels throughout the majority of the U.S.

citations.claim: 10-K Item 1: Shell egg prices use market-based, cost-based, and hybrid arrangements.
citations.excerpt: We sell our shell eggs at prices based on formulas that take into account, in varying ways, one of the independently quoted regional wholesale market prices for shell eggs, our costs of production, such as grain-based, or hybrid models which include elements of cost of production and wholesale market prices.

citations.claim: 10-K Item 1A: Wholesale shell egg market prices fluctuate widely and are outside the company’s control.
citations.excerpt: Our operating results are significantly affected by wholesale shell egg market prices, which fluctuate widely and are outside our control.

citations.claim: 10-K Item 1A: Feed costs are the largest element of shell egg production cost and depend on factors outside the company’s control.
citations.excerpt: Feed costs are the largest element of our shell egg production cost, typically exceeding 50% of our total farm production costs.

citations.claim: 10-K Item 1A: HPAI outbreaks have affected the company’s facilities, including its Maryland pullet facility in March 2026.
citations.excerpt: For example, during the third and fourth quarters of fiscal 2024, we experienced HPAI outbreaks within our facilities located in Kansas and Texas, and in March of 2026 we experienced a HPAI outbreak within our pullet facility in Maryland, resulting in the depopulation of approximately 352,000 pullets.

citations.claim: 10-K Item 1A: The company has significant customer concentration.
citations.excerpt: Our top three customers accounted for an aggregate of 43.1%, 49.2% and 49.0% of our net sales for fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024, respectively.

citations.claim: 10-K Item 1A: Walmart accounted for 30.0% of fiscal 2026 net sales.
citations.excerpt: Our largest customer, Walmart Inc. (including Sam's Club), accounted for 30.0%, 33.6% and 34.0% of net sales dollars for fiscal 2026, 2025 and 2024, respectively.

citations.claim: 10-K Item 1A: The company faces risks integrating prepared-food businesses and brands it acquires.
citations.excerpt: Accordingly, we have experienced and in the future may experience unexpected challenges in integrating and managing the prepared foods businesses and brands that we acquire from time to time.

citations.claim: 10-K Item 7: Fiscal 2026 net sales and net income.
citations.excerpt: For fiscal 2026, we recognized net sales of $2.9 billion and net income of $316.7 million.

citations.claim: 10-K Item 7: Fiscal 2026 net sales declined primarily because conventional shell egg prices fell as the layer population recovered.
citations.excerpt: The decrease was primarily due to the decrease in prices for conventional shell egg, as the layer population recovered in 2025 from the recent HPAI outbreaks, partially offset by sales growth due to acquisitions made during fiscal 2026, particularly Echo Lake Foods.

citations.claim: 10-K Item 7: Average conventional shell egg prices declined 50.9% in fiscal 2026.
citations.excerpt: Our average conventional shell egg price per dozen for fiscal 2026 declined 50.9% compared to fiscal 2025.

citations.claim: 10-K Item 7: Prepared foods sales and their share of net sales in fiscal 2026.
citations.excerpt: In fiscal 2026, prepared foods accounted for $244.8 million or 8.4% of our net sales.

citations.claim: 10-K Item 7: Management attributes recent wholesale egg price declines primarily to improved supply.
citations.excerpt: We believe the recent decline in wholesale egg prices primarily reflects improved egg supply, following disruptions associated with HPAI in fiscal year 2025.

citations.claim: 10-K Item 7: Management reports a segment-reporting reorganization effective in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026.
citations.excerpt: Effective in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, the Company determined its operations are organized into three reportable operating segments: (1) Conventional Shell Eggs; (2) Specialty Shell Eggs; and (3) Prepared Foods.
